story.title: Trump and Putin Meet Ahead of Trilateral Talks with Xi Jinping in China
story.summary: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China, shaking hands as they prepare for their first trilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The meeting comes amid discussions on global security, energy, and finance. While the Kremlin indicated an informal meeting took place, it remains unclear how the ongoing war in Ukraine will be addressed during the talks.

explore_lenses.label: What is actually scheduled for November 19?
explore_lenses.title: A confirmed trilateral, with limited time
explore_lenses.summary: China’s Foreign Ministry has formally announced a November 19 China-Russia-U.S. summit in Shenzhen during the APEC leaders’ meeting. Reporting citing U.S. and Russian officials also indicates that Trump and Putin are expected to hold separate talks, but Moscow has characterized them as short of full-scale negotiations.

claims.text: China’s Foreign Ministry announced on November 16 that Xi Jinping would hold a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen on November 19.
APEC’s official site says the 2026 Economic Leaders’ Meeting is scheduled for Shenzhen on November 19, placing the three-way meeting alongside a broader Asia-Pacific economic gathering.

Reuters reported, citing Kremlin officials, that a Trump-Putin meeting is expected after the APEC plenary and that the trilateral session has one hour allocated; the Kremlin said no full-scale bilateral negotiations were planned.

points: China’s Foreign Ministry announced on November 16 that Xi Jinping would hold a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen on November 19.
APEC’s official site says the 2026 Economic Leaders’ Meeting is scheduled for Shenzhen on November 19, placing the three-way meeting alongside a broader Asia-Pacific economic gathering.

Reuters reported, citing Kremlin officials, that a Trump-Putin meeting is expected after the APEC plenary and that the trilateral session has one hour allocated; the Kremlin said no full-scale bilateral negotiations were planned.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: No jointly agreed agenda, readout format, or deliverables had been publicly released as of November 18.
explore_lenses.note: Researched context; forecasts and viewpoints are labeled and attributed.

explore_lenses.label: What do China and Russia want from the meeting?
explore_lenses.title: Beijing and Moscow stress strategic coordination
explore_lenses.summary: The Xi-Putin meeting before the trilateral produced a detailed public account focused on closer China-Russia cooperation, trade and energy, and a multipolar international order. Those are stated positions of the two governments, not evidence that the three-way meeting will produce agreement.

claims.text: China’s Foreign Ministry said Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen on November 18; Xi called for deeper all-round cooperation and a more stable, predictable environment for bilateral investment and business.
Putin said Russia was ready to deepen cooperation with China in trade, energy and education and to strengthen what he termed “back-to-back” strategic coordination.
China’s foreign ministry described the purpose of the three-way summit as an exchange on global peace and strategic stability among major powers.

points: China’s Foreign Ministry said Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen on November 18; Xi called for deeper all-round cooperation and a more stable, predictable environment for bilateral investment and business.
Putin said Russia was ready to deepen cooperation with China in trade, energy and education and to strengthen what he termed “back-to-back” strategic coordination.
China’s foreign ministry described the purpose of the three-way summit as an exchange on global peace and strategic stability among major powers.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The public Chinese account of the Xi-Putin meeting does not identify any shared China-Russia position on a Ukraine settlement or U.S.-China trade disputes.

explore_lenses.label: Will Ukraine be a substantive agenda item?
explore_lenses.title: Ukraine is likely to arise, but no agreed role is public
explore_lenses.summary: Ukraine has been identified by U.S. and Russian-side officials as a possible discussion topic, while China has kept its public description broad. The available official statements do not establish whether Ukraine will receive dedicated negotiating time or yield any concrete outcome.

claims.text: CBS reported that Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin and Xi discussed Ukraine on November 18, and that Trump and Putin might also discuss it.

When asked whether Ukraine would be covered at the trilateral, China’s Foreign Ministry said only that the leaders would exchange views on important issues bearing on global peace and that further information would be released later.

CBS reported that Trump said the leaders would discuss denuclearization, Iran and Ukraine, while an unnamed official had previously said Ukraine was not expected to be discussed—showing that public descriptions of the agenda have not been fully consistent.

points: CBS reported that Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin and Xi discussed Ukraine on November 18, and that Trump and Putin might also discuss it.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: There is no public indication that Ukraine, which is not represented at the meeting, has accepted or been presented with any proposal from the three leaders.

story_report.summary: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin held an informal meeting in China ahead of planned three-way talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to the Kremlin. The leaders are expected to address global security, energy and finance, although public descriptions of the agenda differ. The encounter set the stage for a China-Russia-U.S. summit in Shenzhen alongside the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting, with no full-scale U.S.-Russia negotiations planned.

sections.heading: Shenzhen summit follows Xi-Putin meeting
sections.body: China’s Foreign Ministry said Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen on November 18, before the scheduled trilateral gathering. Xi called for broader China-Russia cooperation and a more stable, predictable environment for investment and business, while Putin said Russia was prepared to deepen cooperation in trade, energy and education. China has described the three-way meeting as an exchange among major powers on global peace and strategic stability.

sections.heading: Ukraine remains an uncertain agenda item
sections.body: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin and Xi discussed Ukraine, and CBS reported that Trump and Putin might also address the war. Trump said denuclearization, Iran and Ukraine would be discussed, but CBS also reported that an unnamed official had previously said Ukraine was not expected to be on the agenda. China’s Foreign Ministry did not confirm the subject, saying only that the leaders would exchange views on important issues affecting global peace.

unresolved.text: No jointly agreed agenda, readout format or concrete deliverables for the trilateral meeting had been publicly released as of November 18.
There was no public indication that Ukraine had accepted or been presented with any proposal from the three leaders, and Ukraine is not represented at the meeting.

related_stories.title: Israel Initiates Ground Operation in Central Gaza Amid Ceasefire Tensions
related_stories.summary: The Israeli military has launched a new ground operation in central Gaza, specifically targeting Hamas infrastructure. This operation, which occurred west of the Yellow Line, has led to the displacement of numerous Palestinians from their shelters. The military claims the action is necessary to eliminate threats to its troops, while Hamas has condemned the incursion as a violation of the ceasefire established in October 2025.

While the full agenda has not been disclosed, the talks are expected to address trade tensions and advancements in artificial intelligence as well.

related_stories.title: Irish Man Charged with Destroying U.S. Military Plane During Protest
related_stories.summary: Daithí O’Corrain has been charged with destroying a U.S. military aircraft valued at $60 million during a protest. Supporters claim his actions were a political demonstration against U.S. military involvement in conflicts such as the war with Iran and military aid to Israel. The incident reportedly involved an hours-long raid, as described by the FBI.
